name: Deep Sea Glow
summary: The abyssal sea floor at night, lit only by living light: glowing jellies, kelp and coral, marine snow and blue depth fog.
description: A dark navy sea floor of sand ripples, terraced rock shelves and brine pools, with kelp forests, coral, tube-worm gardens and whale bones – and no light except what lives there. Every creature and plant carries its own soft cyan, teal, violet or pink glow: photophores along bodies, polyp tips, gas bulbs, a pulsing jelly bell, an anglerfish lure. The single warm note is the helmet lamp of a small diver. Marine snow drifts past in three parallax layers, faint caustics and light shafts fall from far above, and a blue depth fog swallows the edges of the frame. Unlike hard neon line art, the glow here is soft, organic and always attached to something alive.
bestFor: horror games about light and darkness
night or deep-space style worlds with glowing life
avoidFor: colour-coded puzzle games that need warm hues
projects that need hard graphic line art

difficulty.why: Each new asset is a dark body with a thin cold rim light plus a few bright emissive spots; the shared bake (blurred halo + floor light pool) makes it glow, so drawing is quick. The care goes into restraint: deciding which few spots emit, keeping bodies dark but still readable, giving every creature type its own glow colour and silhouette, and keeping the overdraw of halos and full-screen layers low.

technique.resolution: Native display resolution. Characters baked at 5 px per world unit, props and effects at 4–6 px per unit, ground chunks of 256 units at up to 2.5 px per unit. Fog, light shafts and caustics live in a half-resolution layer blitted nearest-neighbour – they are soft by nature.
technique.summary: Paint every subject twice at bake time: once as the visible body, once with only its light-emitting parts. The emissive pass is blurred (3.2 units wide + 0.9 units tight) into a halo that also carries a flat light pool on the floor, and is added onto the body with 'lighter'. At runtime a creature or prop is one drawImage; the main character keeps its halo separate so it can bloom on top.
technique.linework: No outlines. Bodies are separated by tone and glow: a 0.4–0.75 unit cold rim light (rgba(150,196,255,.42)) on the upper edge of dark forms, 0.3–0.45 unit emissive seams, rims and tentacles, and 0.2–1.0 unit glowing dots. Round caps and joins everywhere – nothing is angular except teeth and crystal-like sponge lattices.
technique.shading: Soft gradients only: radial gradients from a lit side to a near-black edge (anglerfish #2a4068 → #070c18, jelly bell rgba(255,222,250,.95) → rgba(112,52,192,.72)), linear gradients for suits, tanks and bones. Translucent bodies (jelly bells, sponges, fins) at 45–80 % opacity.
technique.lighting: There is no sun. Light comes from living things and the helmet lamp: emissive spots with blurred halos, coloured light pools on the sand under every glowing subject (flat ellipses 0.42 high), a warm volumetric lamp cone and its floor pool. Ground lighting is a faint cold top-left light that only shows on rock lips and ripple crests.
technique.texture: Per-pixel ground: two lookups of one tileable fbm noise tile (128 and 512 units period) for sand grain and mottling, sine sand ripples, terraced rock bands. Elsewhere no texture – the softness comes from blur, gradients and fog.

paletteRules: The scene is ~85 % near-black navy (#040b18 to #1f2f48); glow colours cover only a few percent of the pixels but carry all the contrast.
Glow colours are cold and saturated: cyan, teal, violet, pink, rose, mint – each bright spot gets a white-mixed core (75–85 % towards white) and a falloff in its own colour.
One warm colour only: the helmet lamp (#fff1c8 / #ffc46b). Nothing else in the world is warm, so the main character is always found by its lamp.
Every creature type owns one glow colour: small jelly pink, fast fish cyan, large anglerfish violet + mint lure. Props reuse the palette but never with the same intensity as creatures.
Dark bodies are never pure black: they are navy or violet-black with a cold rim light, so they read as shapes against the floor.
No greens, oranges, reds or greys as surface colours; no white surfaces except tiny highlights and teeth.

world.summary: An abyssal sea floor at night, built per pixel from smooth noise fields and topped with vector decals: dark navy sand with patchy ripples, violet-black silt basins, terraced rock shelves with lit lips, glowing microbial mats, worm trails, burrows, pebbles, shells, sea stars and brine pools with a glowing rim.
layers: Fields on a 4-unit grid (bilinear per pixel): rock (fbm 330 u, domain-warped), silt (fbm 640 u), ripple warp and ripple direction (fbm 170 / 900 u), macro light (fbm 210 u), ripple patches (fbm 150 u); noise detail from one 256 px tileable fbm tile sampled at 2 and 0.5 texels per unit.

Sand: #07101f → #162842 by macro light and grain; ripples sin((x·cos a + y·sin a)·0.66 + warp) (wavelength ≈ 9.5 u) only inside ripple patches – bright crests towards #2c4a6e at up to 50 %, troughs darkened by up to 26 %.
Silt basins where the silt field < 0.43 (fully at 0.36): #09091b → #1a1838 mottling, ripples reduced to 20 %.

Rock shelves where the rock field > 0.6: 24 terraces per field unit; inside a step the tone ramps #060a13 → #1f2f48, the first 16 % after a step is the lip, brightened by the top-left light (dot of the field gradient with (0.45, 0.85)), the last 7 % is a dark crevice, the outer edge gets a #547aa6 rim; a 0.035 band outside the shelf is darkened by up to 60 % as contact shadow.

Decals: worm and sea-cucumber trails (dotted double lines, 14–26 steps of 3.2 u), pebbles (0.6–1.5 u), burrows with a raised rim and sometimes a teal glowing tip, shells, brittle stars and sea stars in pink/violet with a soft pool, microbial mats (13–28 u wide teal/cyan/violet pools with 30–70 glowing dots), 0.16–0.38 u plankton specks, barnacle glints on rock lips.

Brine pools (one chance per 560-unit cell): an organic blob (r 34–60 u, two sine harmonics, 0.62 high) with a dark crust, 140 mussels on the shore, a near-black gradient surface with faint concentric ripples and a violet-cyan rim drawn as three additive strokes (7 / 3 / 0.6 u at 5 / 12 / 55 %).
At runtime only: short light pulses on the floor – about 45 % of 46-unit cells flash once every 2.6–6.6 s in one of the four glow colours.

characters.summary: The main character is a small diver (~18 u wide, ~31 u tall): a dome helmet of dark blue glass with a cute warm-lit face inside, a navy suit with glowing cyan seams, a chest light and wrist light, a grey air tank with a mint indicator, flippers with glowing edges and a warm helmet lamp that throws a soft cone and a floor pool ahead. The creatures hover above the floor and glow in their own colour: a small pink jellyfish (~17 × 22 u) with a pulsing bell, rim dots and trailing tentacles; a fast cyan lantern fish (~21 × 9 u) with a big ringed eye and rows of photophores; and a large dark anglerfish (~41 × 30 u) with needle teeth, a small mint eye, violet lateral dots and a swaying lure on a rod.
rules: Bodies stay dark (navy, violet-black, translucent pink); glow lives only in a few emissive features per creature – rim dots, photophores, teeth, eye, lure, seams.
Silhouette tells the type: dome + tentacles, slim horizontal fish, huge round body with jaws. Colour confirms it: pink, cyan, violet + mint.

Every creature has a matching light pool on the sand below it (2.3 / 2.6 / 1.9 × its radius, alpha 0.3 / 0.22 / 0.18), baked into its sprite; the anglerfish adds a live mint pool under its swaying lure.
Creatures hover: jelly bob 1.6 u at 1.4 rad/s, fish 0.9 u at 3.1 rad/s, anglerfish 1.4 u at 0.9 rad/s – nothing stands on the ground except the diver.
The diver is the only warm light. Its halo stays a separate additive layer (alpha 1.1) so it always blooms over neighbours; creatures have their halo pre-composited into one sprite.
Facing is a mirrored copy; flash and hurt states are tinted silhouettes (#e6fffb aqua-white, #ff5c9a pink) added on top, never a colour change of the body.
Spawning creatures emerge from the dark (alpha = t², glow at 1.8 t) inside a shrinking light ring; dissolving creatures rise 6 u, grow 30 % and fade into a burst of plankton.

props.summary: Sea-floor life and remains, all dark-bodied with a few glowing parts and a baked light pool: tall kelp strands with teal gas bulbs (in forests of 3–6), branching coral with pink polyp tips, fan coral, tube-worm clusters with rose plumes, whale bones (rib cage and skull with jaw) dotted with pink worm colonies, anemones in cyan, violet or pink, basalt rocks with cyan barnacles and a sea star or urchin, a hydrothermal vent chimney with a violet mouth glow, and glass sponges (lattice vase, violet barrel).
rules: Props are darker and dimmer than creatures: emissive parts are small dots and tips, the rest is navy, violet-black or dim bone.
Each prop bakes a flat light pool under its base in its glow colour (alpha 0.1–0.32) – that pool is what plants it on the floor.

Placement follows the ground: kelp forests in their own noise field, coral, rocks, anemones and vents on rock shelves, whale falls, sponges and tube worms in silt, nothing inside a brine pool or within 95 units of the start.

Motion is slow and organic: kelp cycles through 8 baked bend frames (stalk tip ±4.5 u), anemones sway with a small shear, vents emit dark smoke puffs and rising bubbles, light spots on anemones, tube worms and vents pulse.
Glass sponges and jelly-like parts are translucent (fill alpha 0.16–0.22) with a bright lattice or rim – they should look like glowing glass, not solid objects.

effects.name: Glowing projectile
effects.how: A 2-unit white-to-cyan orb with its own halo, a 22-unit tapered cyan tail (blurred gradient wedge) that grows from 20 % to full length in 0.1 s, and three tiny aqua plankton sparks wobbling behind it – all additive.

effects.name: Plankton burst
effects.how: When a creature dissolves: 22 (large: 38) glowing motes in the creature's colours drift outwards with heavy water drag (3.2) and float slowly upwards (buoyancy −9), living 0.8–1.6 s; plus a 0.25 s core flash, 4–9 rising bubbles and a dark ink puff for the large creature.

effects.name: Light rings
effects.how: Additive ellipses drawn twice (3.6 × width at 22 % alpha, then the line itself): flat floor rings 0.42 high that expand with ease-out (impact, collect, dash, glow-up) and upright circles at body height for impacts.

effects.name: Bubble streams
effects.how: A baked bubble sprite (thin pale ring, soft inner glow, white highlight) that rises with buoyancy (−36), wobbles ±0.8 u and fades; streams from the diver's helmet every 1.3–2.6 s, along a dash, from vents and on bursts.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small: a teal-white plankton orb (core r 1.55 + ring r 2.7) bobbing 0.9 u, 4.5 u above a small teal pool. Large: a 3.3-unit pearl with a white-violet gradient, softer halo and a rotating four-point glint.

effects.name: Orbiting moon jelly
effects.how: A tiny aqua-white jellyfish (bell 3.4–4.2 u, four-leaf gonads, six tentacles, 4 pulse frames) circling the main character 10 u above the floor, trailing a fading arc of seven segments and a small cyan floor pool.

effects.name: Impact spark
effects.how: Six short-lived motes (aqua-white + creature colour) bursting from the hit point, a 0.14 s aqua flash and a small upright ring; the body itself is overlaid with its aqua-white silhouette at up to 75 % for ~0.15 s.

effects.name: Glow-up
effects.how: A teal light column (20 × 98 u gradient), three rising ellipse rings, 24 motes floating up in the four glow colours, 12 bubbles and two wide floor rings in teal and violet.

atmosphere.summary: Underwater depth instead of sky: soft light shafts and two layers of drifting caustics from far above, marine snow in three parallax depths (including big out-of-focus specks), coloured light pools instead of shadows, and a blue depth fog that darkens and swallows the frame edges.
rules: No cast shadows: only a faint dark contact smudge under the diver (and the anglerfish); everything else gets coloured light pools on the sand.

Depth fog: radial gradient from 26 % of the short side to 58 % of the diagonal – rgba(4,16,34,0) → .26 at 42 % → rgba(3,11,24,.68) at 78 % → rgba(1,5,12,.9); plus a faint lighter murky band (rgba(30,92,130,.12)) at the top 40 %.

Light shafts: four slanted beams (top widths 6–10 % of the screen, widening 2.4×, alpha 0.09–0.16 fading to 0 at the bottom), blurred once and baked at 80 % into the static fog layer – the moving caustics give them life.

Caustics: one 256 px tileable tile of domain-warped Worley cell edges (f2 − f1 < 0.11), drawn twice in world space – 205 u and 282 u per tile (second layer rotated 90°) drifting in different directions – at 7 % and 5.5 %, so the bright web slowly shimmers.

Marine snow: 84 tiny specks (0.3–0.75 u, parallax 1.06), 42 small (0.65–1.25 u, parallax 1.32) and 12 big blurry bokeh discs (2.6–4.6 u, parallax 1.95, 14 % alpha), sinking 3–7.5 u/s, swaying and twinkling.

Fog, shafts and caustics are composed in one half-resolution layer (a static fog + shaft base copied in, two translation-only caustic fills from tiles pre-scaled to the layer) and drawn with a single nearest-neighbour full-screen blit per frame; snow is drawn before it so the fog also swallows distant specks.
On a bright foreign floor (style mixes) the separate halos are scaled down by ground luminance so glows do not blow out to white.

ui.summary: A submersible instrument panel: dark gunmetal-teal glass panels with rounded corners, four rivet dots and a double bezel ring (inner cyan line + outer dark ring), glowing glass-tube bars with a sheen and drifting bubbles in the fill, a depth-gauge tick scale under the top bar, a circular sonar screen with concentric rings, crosshair, blips and a rotating sweep around the timer, porthole-framed card icons and Exo 2 / Quantico / Comfortaa type with soft glow.

motion: Everything drifts slowly – water has drag: particles use drag 2.6–3.2 and float upwards (negative gravity) instead of falling.

Main character: 8-frame walk with flippers kicking ±3.1 u, body bob 0.9 u, arms swinging ±0.75 rad; idle floats 0.7 u at 2.1 rad/s; dash tilts the figure 0.62 rad forward into a swimming pose with three halo afterimages 8 u apart; exhaled bubble clusters of 3–5 rise from the helmet valve every 1.3–2.6 s.

Jellyfish: 8 pulse frames at ~0.85 cycles/s – the bell narrows from 8.5 to 6.2 u, rises 1.4 u and the tentacles stretch; lantern fish: 6 tail frames at 2.4 cycles/s with a two-step speed streak; anglerfish: 8 frames of jaw opening and fin flaps, lure swaying ±1.6 u and pulsing.
Lights breathe instead of blinking: floor pulses rise and fall in 30 % of their 2.6–6.6 s period, polyp and plume spots pulse at 1.6 rad/s, the lamp flickers ±8 %.
Kelp bends through 8 baked frames over ~7.7 s; the two caustic layers drift at 2.8 and 2.8 u/s in different directions; marine snow sinks 3–7.5 u/s.
The sonar sweep rotates once every 4.5 s, its blips pulse every 2.2 s, bubbles drift through the top bar fill every 3 s.
do: Keep 85 % of the image near-black navy and let a few small, bright, living lights carry the picture.
Paint bodies dark with a thin cold rim light from above, then add emissive dots, seams and tips – never light a whole body evenly.
Give every glowing subject a coloured light pool on the sand; it replaces shadows and grounds hovering creatures.
Give each creature type its own glow colour and silhouette (pink dome, cyan fish, violet giant with a mint lure).
Bake halos once (blur at init) and add them with 'lighter'; pre-composite halos into the sprite for anything that appears in numbers.
Use slow, organic motion: pulses, sways, drifting snow, rising bubbles – water slows everything.
Frame the scene with depth: fog at the edges, parallax snow, faint shafts and caustics from far above.
dont: Don't draw hard outlines or neon line art – this style's glow is soft, blurred and attached to living things.
Don't light the floor evenly or brighten the ground above ~#2c4a6e; the sand must stay darker than every creature.
Don't add warm colours to the world – the helmet lamp is the only warm light.
Don't use ctx.filter or shadowBlur per frame; blur only at bake time.
Don't stack many full-screen layers (fog, shafts, caustics each at full resolution) – compose them small and blit once.
Don't make creatures fully transparent ghosts: their bodies need enough opacity and a rim to read on the dark floor.
Don't fill the water with too many bright particles; marine snow is faint (alpha 0.1–0.55) and tiny.
performance: Baked once in init (~0.4 s): main character 8 walk + idle + dash, jellyfish 8, lantern fish 6, anglerfish 8 frames (each a body pass, an emissive pass, two blurs, flash and hurt tints and mirrored copies; creature halos pre-composited), collectibles, projectile head and tail, 4 moon-jelly frames, 24 kelp bend frames and 13 other prop sprites, glow sprites per colour, one caustic tile. Ground: generator chunks of 256 units (~60–100 ms each, split into ~57 steps of at most a few ms): one field grid, one per-pixel pass with lazily interpolated channels, decal passes and brine pools. Per frame: one drawImage per prop, creature and collectible (halos AND floor light pools are pre-composited and sprites are cropped to their visible pixels), a small pulse glow for anemones, tube worms and vents, ~140 snow sprites, one half-resolution compose (copy of the static fog + shaft base, two translation-only caustic fills) and a single nearest-neighbour full-screen blit. The fill rate of full-screen layers is the main cost to watch: in the benchmark the frame cost is on par with the neon style.
